utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning -- thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, Alex Demirdjian, and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Ms. Tatjana Savic appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic and Aleksandar Aleksic appearing for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand there are a number of matters to be dealt with before the witness comes back in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I notified the Registrar I need to make a submission. Your Honours will remember that on the 28th of April, 2011, the Stanisic Defence filed the motion to compel the Prosecution to comply with the Rule 66(B). Now, Your Honours, we file -- we requested the disclosure based on Rule 66(B) from the Office of the Prosecutor concerning all upcoming witnesses on 20th of April, 2011. We got the reply from the Office of the Prosecutor the very next day, the 21st of April, where the Prosecution wouldn't comply with the -- with our request. We filed a motion to compel and it's pending before the Trial Chamber. Now, Your Honours, we are halfway through our case now. This is our -- the next witness is our witness number four and it's not like we have 80 witnesses; we have eight or nine witnesses. Therefore, we -- we need the decision before we call the witness to the stand, the decision on our motion to compel. Because if it's -- if the decision -- if the decision is not there, then we will have the very same problems that we had with the -- with the -- with Andrija Bjelosevic, the disclosure of the documents which we have never seen, and so on and so forth. Now, we agreed to move on with our expert witnesses because we understood that they are expert witnesses and we called them before the -- before the decision was -- was taken, the ruling was taken on our motion. But now we are in position that we need to have that before we call our witness. That is my submission. Thank you very much. Our next witness, I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The Chamber, of course, is not unmindful of the urgency of this and appreciates your concerns. But the -- I would only say at this point that the matter is not as straightforward as may have first appeared, and it is a decision which we expect to be able to issue shortly. More than that, I'm afraid I'm unable to be more helpful to you at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we have noted your concerns and taken them on board, Mr. Zecevic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours I just want to deal with one matter where we've reached agreement with the Defence. At the Defence conference, we had a discussion about certain documents, criminal reports, which may or may not have appeared in the Doboj KU book. I'm happy to say we've now reached agreement, and the Defence are prepared to admit - I'll read this slowly - that criminal reports 1D -- with the exhibit numbers 1D355, 356, 357, 360, 361 and 362 all appear in the KU Doboj book with the exhibit number 1D358.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. And could the witness be escort back to the stand, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, good morning to you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before Ms. Korner resumes, I give you the usual reminder as to your solemn declaration. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, I would like to be able to finish asking you questions today, so I would be most grateful if you could just keep your answers short and answer the questions. I want to begin this morning, please, by just asking you to look one more time at a list of payroll -- a payroll for Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we have on the screen, please, document 20108, which is at tab 24F. I'll repeat the number: 20108. Your Honours, I'm told, yet again, there's a technical problem which is about the worst possible time. And it's, of course, important that the accused see the document. I hope that this technical problem can be sorted out asap.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I am afraid also the witness needs to see the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I know. We can do it in Sanction, Your Honours. This obviously can't go on, so I hope somebody will come and fix this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Do you see the document now, Mr. Bjelosevic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is payment for May --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I believe the witness said he doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, he doesn't. Oh, sorry. Could somebody perhaps turn Sanction on for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is a payment list for the police detachment staff, and you'll -- for May. And you'll recall we discussed that last week, the division of the police into detachments. And number 5, Milutin Blaskovic. Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Milutin Blaskovic was a chief of the police detachment and he retired sometime in 1991. I know who he is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In fact, if we go to the third page in English and second page in B/C/S, we can see that it's -- third page in English. Thanks. We can see there the list of the police detachment staff. Yes. Thank you. Your Honours, in the light of the discussions, this is a brand new document. I mean, actually brand new received very recently. But can I have it marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2331, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now I want to go back to where we were on Friday, please, when we were looking at documents during the period when you said that the CSB Doboj was not functioning. That is to say, between the 3rd of May and the end of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we have a look, please, now at document 20007. Are we still having to use Sanction? Right. Tab number 24.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's a letter dated the 30th of May, Mr. Bjelosevic. Is that signed by you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's not the contents, really, in which I'm interested. So on the 30th of May, you were obviously at the CSB Doboj to be able to sign this letter?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may have been on the 30th or a day or two later, I don't know. But I did sign this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, Your Honours, may this be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I could only comment. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, if there's something you want to say and provided you say it shortly.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very briefly, yes. We can see from the letterhead that this is the National Security Service, and this segment was operational all the time as the National Security Department or state security, as it was called in different periods.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just have this marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2332, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, what you said about this originally when you were asked questions, and this is transcript page 19608, is that there was a meeting of the Crisis Staff, and it was agreed, you said, that since the centre did not have any territory, and there -- and there was a lack of personnel for it to be possible for departments to function, namely, the milicija, the crime police, administrative department and so on, it was decided that the public security station should function until further notice with its own elements and that the personnel who remained who were ethnic Serbs within the centre should be re-directed to the station so that the station could function in the best possible way. And that is, indeed, what was done: "Therefore, since then, not a single department in the CSB has" - it says "hasn't," but I think it must be "has" - "functioned except for the communications department. The centres for communications is a single one, and it is used for the CSB and for the station?" That's what you said; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A single centre, both for the SJB and the CSB, and for the state security department or national security. That's a single centre. But we are talking about the National Security Department which continued functioning. However, all these I have just listed were not operational. And whoever claims the contrary should specify which was operational at which time and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. This, you said, was done by agreement at a meeting of the Doboj Crisis Staff; that's right, is it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if "agreement" is the right word. If a decision was taken or an order issued, then that's something that has executive power.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm -- I'm quoting you the word you used. Are you now saying it was an order by the Crisis Staff as opposed to an agreed course of action?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said originally that it was done pursuant to instructions. You were able to see the document, and it reads "it is hereby ordered," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. I'm not going to go on and put to you what you said originally. Now I want to you have a look, please, at another document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 20102. Tab -- oh, tab 106. Sorry, I didn't hear that. Tab 106.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Do you recognise that book?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Could it be enlarged?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I tell you what, I can give you a better copy.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still cannot make out the text on the label.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise for the fact that somebody is actually -- when this was being photographed, somebody actually wrote in English what it was. Oh, can we -- he's got the -- we can try and zoom in on the title a bit more.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot read the text.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, are you familiar with the on-site investigation book, Mr. Bjelosevic, from the CSB?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the on-site investigation reports? I know that such reports were made and photographs were part of it, if that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's go to, please, the first page. Second page, sorry. Does that show, on the 14th of May, that there was an on-site investigation on a murder that had been committed with a fire-arm?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if we go to the last column in that -- for you that book --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But we need to go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Does that show that the on-site investigation was carried out by Inspector Stankovic and Miladinovic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which number is that? You mean 5?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Number 1 on the list. And it's column 13 in the book.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Stankovic, Miladinovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And on the 20th of May, the 22nd of May, the 8th of June, the 10th of June, were on-site investigations carried out?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you give me the number for the first column? It will be easier for me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think it says number 1, which we dealt with. Number 2, 20th of May.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Number 3, 22nd of May.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Number 4, 8th of June.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And number 5, 10th of June.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, again, if you go in each of those to column 13 - if we can move to the next page again in English - we see the inspectors who carried out these on-site investigations. So can we take it from that, Mr. Bjelosevic, that the -- there were members of the CSB working and that on-site investigations were being carried out?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That conclusion would not be justified because all these investigators at the time were members of the SJB.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is -- the on-site investigations were carried out by the CSB, weren't they? This is what this book is headed, and these gentlemen were all members of the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Ms. Korner. It is probably the haste with which are you examining the witness. But you haven't established whether the witness knows this book. You posed the question but it was -- it was not responded.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: My understanding is whether he knows it or not, that's what the book is actually entitled.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But the problem is that this piece of paper which is -- which we see on the photograph is not a part of the book. It was done probably by your investigators.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's the front of the book, as I understand it, which, I agree, is very difficult to read. However, if there's a dispute that this is the CSB Doboj's crime investigation log-book, then, of course, I will call evidence to establish that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Bjelosevic, I've omitted -- you didn't answer: Have you seen this book before?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have not seen it, and I wish to point out, once again, that during the time-period we are discussing, the CSB did not have a crime police department, and whoever claims the contrary, then have him say to me who the chiefs of the department were -- was and who the inspectors or investigators of the department were, and so on. The names I have seen here were members of the SJB Doboj at that time. And I really cannot make out the letters on the label on the cover. I have never held this book in my hands. But I stand by what I said with regard to the staff of the CSB. You may be drawing parallels here, analogies, because the name of Veljko Solaja is mentioned here. Veljko Solaja once worked at the CSB once the crime police department was established, and some other inspectors, too. But at this time, it was the way I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's make this clear. Are you saying that although in normal times, Stankovic, Solaja and the others would have been members of the CSB? Because the CSB wasn't operating, they were, at that stage, you say, members of the SJB?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In May and June, they were members of the SJB. And they took part in this as members of that station's department.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm suggesting to you, you know, Mr. Bjelosevic, that, in fact, the CSB, with or without your assistance, was actually operating. And that's the truth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you for someone to tell me who the chief of the crime investigation service was at the centre at the time, who the inspectors were, who the chief of department for finance was, or the chief of the aliens department, and so on, and then we can have a discussion about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... 65 ter, please, 20109, which is tab 24G. Thank you. Your Honours, could I also ask that this volume be marked for identification. As I say, if there's a dispute that this is the CSB book, I'll call evidence about it later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2333, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we see there, please, the payment for May 1992, Crime Service Doboj. And if -- it's dated 8th of June. And if we go, please, to numbers 9 and 15 on this list.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Do you still stand by your answer that the CSB Doboj, in May and June, had no crime service with the inspectors that we've seen?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. This document corroborates what I said. Look at the top of the page. It says "crime service." Look at all these names that are listed here, and do have a look at the lower right-hand corner. It is not type written but I recognise the signature. It is the head of the station, Obren --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the last name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this confirm what I had said all along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, could you repeat the last name for the -- for the interpreter who didn't get it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said who it was that had signed the document. Obren Petrovic. It is his signature. He was chief of the public security station in Doboj at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to move then, please, briefly to your relationship with Mr. Todorovic in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we look, first of all, at tab 14B, which is P2164.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is a description of the takeover from the 1st KK, or, in fact, it was still in the 5 KK, about the takeover of Samac: "... members of the Territorial Defence and MUP of the Serbian municipality took control of the MUP of Bosanski Samac ..." Correct? That was your information as well?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you will allow me, I'd just like to read this. I'm sorry, what was the question? Whether I was -- what, whether I knew about this, right?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether I knew that this had happened?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had found out that this had happened, but I don't know exactly when in that period of time that we're discussing now, the month of April. By then, all communications had been cut off towards Modrica and further on there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Todorovic was then appointed, as you say rightly, by the Crisis Staff as chief of the SJB. When did you find that out?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the corridor was broken through and when there was communication between Samac and Doboj and vice versa, then I gained some more serious knowledge as to what had happened there; namely, that the station had been relocated from its original building which, indeed, had been by the Sava river. It was relocated to the department store that was further in town, because that building, and also the TO building that was in this line of houses, as the municipal building was, were often fired at by the Croat side.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the municipality had relocated as well. And then when the corridor was re-established, I found out what the situation was in Samac. Basically, this is the first information I received. I cannot say exactly on which date that happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, that's all I asked you, and your answer is that you did not know that Todorovic had been appointed chief of the SJB until the opening of the corridor, so the end of June?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I did know. Because, from time to time, there were special telephone lines that were used by the railways and they could be used as well. So I don't exactly -- who I heard this from, but I did know that a certain Todorovic had been appointed, that he was chief of the station there. However, I didn't know who the man was, and I wasn't aware of any other details. So I'm speaking about other knowledge that I had at the time. And I do apologise, I didn't quite understand what it was that you were saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's have a look now, please, at document 20136. Oh, tab 14G.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature at the bottom of Mirko Blazanovic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And this is from the duty operations service, duty officers, Mr. Kopcic and Mr. Blazanovic, dated 18th/19th April, timed at 0820 hours. At about 1500 hours on the 18th of April, the commander of ... Mr. Petrovic informed the CSB that Samac had been blocked by Serbian territorials ... all important facilities being held. 200 persons of Muslim or Croatian ethnicity still in the facilities. Four or five workers are being held in the SJB. Acting Chief Dragan Lukic had been captured. Stevo Todorovic who is the former director of Korpara from Samac has been appointed to chief, and so on and so forth. Are you saying that your two inspectors or duty officers there did not pass the information on to you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying that. I said that I knew this from earlier on, who had been appointed, and now this refreshed my memory. However, details about the work of the station, that I did not know until the month of July, when it was possible to go there. But I did know that a certain Todorovic had been appointed, whom I did not know personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. You see that was the question I asked you, not when you first got to the station, but when you first knew that Todorovic had been appointed. And you agree, do you, that it must have been very shortly after the appointment?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may that be marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, so marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I forgot to ask for the earlier payroll with the 65 ter 20109, to be marked for identification as well. That's the one showing the crime inspectors, Solaja and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Also marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, therefore the exhibit numbers are P2334, marked for identification; and the second exhibit is P2335, marked for identification. The first one is 65 ter 20109. And the second one, 65 ter 20136. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, did you, hearing about this appointment, take any steps at all, before you disappeared off to the military, to either legitimatise his appointment or do anything about it at all?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I couldn't have done anything about any of that. However, to understand the situation better, may I remind you that it was very complex and dynamic in other areas as well, other municipalities, like Derventa. Also here towards Modrica, and so on, there was a general state of chaos that prevailed at the time, and I simply could not have done anything in Samac. It was a war zone that was isolated from us, and one could not reach it anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you make any attempts to see that the information was passed onto your superiors in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information was certainly passed on, on the very same day, when the information bulletin was compiled. It was the month of April. No doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if communications were down on that particular day. But as soon as communication was re-established, that is what went through.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you explained to Mr. Zecevic about the criminal -- the crimes that Mr. Todorovic was committing and what happened in November. When did you become aware that Mr. Todorovic was, in fact, himself committing crimes?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Todorovic was very reserved, as far as the relationship between the station and the centre was concerned. It's only when he left definitely and a bit before that, too, I found out - perhaps this is a harsh word - that he lied a lot about what was going on in Samac. I think that in August inspectors from the CSB went for the first time to see what the situation was down there, and their findings were that the service was not functioning properly. After that, information was sent to the MUP. Then the MUP intervened by way of sending certain instructions, certain inspectors from the MUP headquarters. Then, again, looking into the situation in Samac. And after that, there was very dynamic activity going on around Samac to establish a system of work there. You saw that I made a few attempts to have him replaced, and so on and so forth. However, the picture was fully completed only after he had left the service, when other people had taken over, and when they established what had been happening there. That's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So the question, the original question was, please: When did you discover that Mr. Todorovic was committing crimes? Just requires a simple one-line answer, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first knowledge was related to shortcomings in work. As for crimes, well, only sometime in the autumn. I cannot say anything more specific. However, I knew of his shortcomings already in August and then about the crime, sometime in the autumn.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let's have a look at your various meetings with him, then, shall we? Your diary, please, for the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It is tab 107C.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Have you got your diaries with you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I have it here, and I was told that not everything had been scanned, so I'll let you have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understand it is 20103.03. I'm told that my giving of the tab number wasn't recorded on the transcript. But it is tab 107C.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Does that record a meeting on the 10th of July with the chiefs of the SJBs?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The day before you -- or probably the same day that you went up for the meeting in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, it was the day before the Belgrade meeting. And these are the questions that I wanted to deal with, collecting information from the chiefs so that I could provide information at the meeting that followed, status of the employees, inventory of the materiel supplies, report on work, organisation of communications to see where communications function and where they do not and whether there were any special forces, units, and so on, everything that I asked of them at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We can assume, can we, from this, that having seen Todorovic and heard his report the day before the meeting, you were perfectly satisfied with what he was telling you. Because you didn't explain to Mico Stanisic about him, did you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the questions that I needed for the first meeting with the minister. I needed to know what existed in the region, which services, which stations were functioning, how many employees were there. And then later, at the meeting in Belgrade, I presented, during my own remarks, what they had told me about this time. I could not look into their heads. I just heard what each one of them had to say. I did not agree or disagree with him. You see what the questions were that we discussed on that day. This was by way of preparation of the meeting that followed. And then later, we went into some more in-depth reporting as to their reporting about what the situation was in other areas. I'm saying that practice has shown that he did not tell the truth at these meetings. Inspectors found out that he had not been telling the truth and that the situation was different from the way he had presented it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. My simple question was: You didn't see anything wrong, so you didn't complain about him to Mico Stanisic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because I was not in Samac at the time, and what he said seemed to be all right. And you see which questions that had to do with.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may that be marked for identification, please. Actually, I think there's no objection to these going in. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2336, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you move then, please, now to the 16th of August in your diary, which is 107E, and it is 20103.5. Is that another meeting with Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with Todorovic only. You see who all the attendees were, but he was one of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've told us it was August, or you told the Court when you were answering questions -- Mr. Zecevic, page 19868, it was August that you discovered that -- and you say this was after the inspectors, that there were irregularities going on, as you put them, in Samac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, indeed, you suggested at a meeting with Blagoje Simic that Todorovic should be replaced.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did not come there to utter that sentence, but as soon as he saw what we were talking about, he stopped talking.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who stopped talking?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simic. Simic. He didn't want to listen to us anymore, neither me nor my co-workers who came with me. I think that in my previous testimony I said how he reacted to this, which words he used, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we go in your diary to the page which has Simic -- Todorovic speaking, sorry, which is, in English, the third page.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, was your meeting with Simic before or after this meeting with Todorovic, on the 16th of August?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was after this. I think. I cannot say for sure, but I think it was after this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you're suggesting to Mr. Simic that he should be replaced. Did you make the same suggestion to Mico Stanisic or to Mico Stanisic's assistant for public security?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So this would have been in August of about 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it was August. I think it was later. It was later.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How much later?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps -- I mean, I'm afraid I'll make a mistake. Perhaps the second half of September; I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Why did you wait so long? I mean, it was clear to you by August that this man was wholly unsuitable to be the chief of the SJB in Samac.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am telling you how we came to know how things were functioning there. You see, he is speaking on the 16th of August. What he said -- I mean, on the basis of what he said, it is hard to conclude that there was something wrong. When the inspectors went there, though, because I asked for them to go to all the situation -- to all the stations that were re-established to see what the situation was, and when they saw what the situation was like and when they came back and when they wrote up their reports, then I saw that there were shortcomings there. And then we took things in the right order. First, I asked those who had appointed him to have him replaced because the man showed, according to our initial knowledge, that he really did not find his way there and then that failed. Then we heard more things about the problems that were and then more, so we realised that there were a lot of things that were wrong there and then --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that we were supposed to replace this man. Obviously he could not be head of the station. He could not do that because he did not have the required knowledge and he did not meet any other requirements; moral and others. However, the policy-makers who appointed him did what they did, and you see how he left ultimately.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to go on to that in a moment. But it's all, if I may put it this way, Mr. Bjelosevic, very vague. What was the moral requirement that he did not meet? Wasn't he actually, to your knowledge -- it was being reported to you, he was beating up prisoners personally?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I learned later. But when we speak of moral qualities, how can it be normal for somebody to come to a meeting and lie there? To my mind, that is not a moral person who comes to make a report of the situation and lie, and then I hear from my inspectors that there were problems which he didn't want to speak about. That's what I meant when I mentioned moral qualities. But that only surfaced later, his overall conduct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Later, when, please?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've just told you. Sometime in the Autumn.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, you dealt with all the events of November and the inspectors with Mr. Zecevic. So let's have a look, please, what happens in December. Could you look at your diary, please, for the 15th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it's tab 107G, and it is 20103.07.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, would you offer the -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... certainly, yes. Could I have the last entry in October made an exhibit as well, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 20103.05 shall be given exhibit number P2337. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's August. It's not October, sorry, 16th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. 16th of August. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How come Mr. Todorovic is back in Samac on the 15th of December, 1992, as chief?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how. What do you mean how come he's back?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We went through all the documents about him being removed in November because it was clear to everybody that he was committing crimes, and how the roads were blockaded because of that. But he is still chief of the SJB in December 1992, at which stage everybody knows about the crimes he's been committing, don't they?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, a lot was known already about his offences. And with my co-workers, I was preparing the elements to launch disciplinary proceedings...However, since he never received [an appointment] decision* from the minister, then such proceedings could not be instituted because he had been appointed by another body. And I think that this must have been his last meeting, and after that, he left the service and found employment with the municipality. And somebody else took over the police station as acting chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a really serious mistake in the transcript, and -- or interpretation. But really, really serious. I -- I, indeed, have a big problem with this. Page 24/10, the witness never ever mentioned anything of the kind. 10 and 11. I don't know where it came from. I really don't know. Perhaps we can -- we can listen to the audiotape of this, but I'm really complaining. This is -- this is -- this is a serious -- this is a very serious problem, I think. Because something is put on the record which the witness never ever said, nor mentioned. So it's -- it's not a mistake. It's just ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I agree with Mr. Zecevic. It is important this, and I think the audiotape will have to be listened to. Perhaps that can be done over the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I can carry on. We can come -- I'd like to finish the topic of Samac before the break and then we can go back and listen to this. And then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It may be helpful if the witness could repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think not. If you forgive me, on this occasion, no. I think we should listen to the tape first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Very well. I think I understand, but, yes. Yes, let's --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just complete -- we can come -- I will come back to that once we know exactly what was said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You said that was the last meeting. Can you look, please --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I ask that be admitted and marked, that entry for the 31st -- for the 12th -- 15th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you look, please, at your entry for the 31st of December.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me. I apologise. 65 ter 20103.07 shall be given exhibit number P2338. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, do we see a meeting which includes Mr. Todorovic? It is typed as Sabac but that is obviously Samac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So that wasn't his last meeting because there was another one in December.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, finally, on the topic of Mr. Todorovic -- not finally because we have to come back to it after the break. Could you have a look, please, at P732.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm not sure what the tab number is. I think it's ... 120. Thank you. If we go, please, to page 12, I think it is. It's page 12 in English. It's number 91 on the list under: Medal for services to the nation. Let's see if I can spot it in B/C/S. Yes, it's page -- it says 0296-9864 at the top. That's not the page, sorry. Can you go on, please -- backwards in B/C/S, I think it is. Yep. And number 91 --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that Stevan Todorovic, chief of Samac SJB, getting a medal in -- I think it's 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name under 91 is Stevan Todorovic. And it says that he is chief of the Samac SJB. I don't know what this is about, but I suppose that what you're saying is correct because you have seen the entire document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I can take you back to the front page of this document, in both cases, B/C/S and English. The Official Gazette of Republika Srpska, number 4/93. Looked at Todorovic. We go, please, to the second page in English and the second page, I think, in B/C/S as well, yep, while we're on the topic. At number 12 at the top in B/C/S and halfway down, is that you getting the Karadjordjevic Star, second class?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was decorated with the Karadjordjevic Star, second class. That's a decoration for military accomplishment and merits.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... military -- hold on a moment, please. In B/C/S we have to go back to the previous page, please. These are all policemen, everything single one of them, aren't they: Skipina, Mihic, Radovic, Krsic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But the MUP, that is, the police, also took part in armed combat. I only explained the character of the -- or the nature of the decoration. There are various decorations and the Karadjordjevic Star was awarded for military virtues and merits. That was its full name. Many or, well, certainly a number of MUP members were awarded that decoration.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. But, to your knowledge, when was Mr. Skipina ever involved in any fighting? Or don't you know anything about Mr. Skipina?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Skipina who?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Slobodan Skipina. One of the assistant ministers.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know who Slobodan Skipina is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When was he ever involved in fighting?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't have to take part in fighting directly with a rifle. But he may have done some valuable work in the field of intelligence maybe, and that also affected the armed forces and their armed combat and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is probably an appropriate moment so we can get the transcript checked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, we return in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, before the witness is brought in, we clarified the situation, and I would like to -- but -- to say that my comment which I made was inappropriate. I -- I would like to extend my apologies to the interpreters, because, definitely, there was a mistake in the -- in the translation, and Ms. Korner can read what we had agreed was said. But I understood only when I was reviewing the audiotape I understood how hard their work is, and that the mistake which was made was obviously an honest mistake. So, therefore, I'm sorry. And Ms. Korner can read what the witness actually said. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we had somebody with Mr. Zecevic listening to the tape, and what was said was: "With my co-workers, I was preparing to start disciplinary proceedings. Since he never received his appointment from the minister, and since he was appointed by another body ..." And that's the most -- I think the effect was definitely: We could do nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. And, Mr. Zecevic, the -- I'm sure the interpreters are appreciative of your gracious apology on the record, since your comments had been made on the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, before the break, you were explaining that although you had been preparing disciplinary proceedings against Todorovic, you couldn't take them because he'd been appointed, in effect, by the Crisis Staff. What was to stop Mico Stanisic giving him a retrospective appointment and then taking the disciplinary proceedings, because we know this happened in a number of occasions?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably the fact that his appointment by the minister would amount to the acceptance of the way he worked. I suppose that's it, that he disapproved of the way Stevan Todorovic worked and behaved.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, why wasn't he -- and you may not be able to answer this, but why wasn't he given a retrospective appointment if, as far as you were concerned, until later, when you found out about his crimes and his bad management, why couldn't he have been given a retrospective appointment, say, somewhere between April and whenever you say you found out, September? And if you don't know the answer, say so.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But are you saying that simply because he had been appointed by the Crisis Staff, there was absolutely no legal method to remove a SJB chief who had been committing crimes and not running the police station properly? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to launch disciplinary proceedings, legally speaking --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I understand what you are saying about disciplinary proceedings. But are you saying that he couldn't have been arrested?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you saw how the situation developed when the army arrested him. I think that will be the most telling answer. It was possible, but you saw what happened. The entire municipality leadership raised some military forces, and the police was ordered to block the corridor. I understand you, from your perspective and from the vantage point of today, after so much time it may be difficult to understand. But figuratively speaking, I was in a position to sniff the end of a barrel pointed at my head several times, and it was easy to get killed at those times.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, in fact, Todorovic remained chief of the SJB, didn't he, until 1994, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 1994, that's what I suggest to you, Mr. Bjelosevic. That's how long he was chief of the SJB for.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You don't agree, all right. Finally on Samac, please, can I ask to you to look at this document, which is tab -- sorry. Exhibit 21 -- 20100, 2100, and it's tab 105. If it makes it easier for you, I will give you a large copy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 2100, please. 65 ter number. Sorry, it's 65 ter number. Tab 105.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think the correct 65 ter is 20101. That's tab 105. That's crime report register.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Daily events log-book, Samac. Sorry, my note is in error. 20101.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, while we are waiting for this document to come up on the screen, I'd like to ask you why it was that you couldn't have filed disciplinary proceedings against Mr. Todorovic in any case? Was that because you thought that the Crisis Staff, who had appointed Mr. Todorovic, would not have approved of such proceedings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Crisis Staff wouldn't have approved his replacement. And it didn't. And it -- and disciplinary proceedings is a legal category. Whoever was appointed to a position could be subject to disciplinary proceedings, but if they weren't, then it wasn't possible because it wouldn't be correct legally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So are you saying that the reason why disciplinary proceedings could not have been instituted against Mr. Todorovic was that he hadn't been appointed by the minister. Was that the reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Because there was no ministry decision on his appointment. I'm not a lawyer, but the lawyers that we had at the CSB at the time explained it to me this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So in the period where we know that a number of persons were appointed by the Crisis Staffs, in all those instances, those who had been appointed were immune from disciplinary proceedings. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not all legal proceedings, but disciplinary proceedings, yes, to use your phrase, they were immune because there was no legal foundation for disciplinary proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... can I ask that you be given a printout.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, again I have to apologise for the fact it was photographed with a sticker on it, to show what it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that book, Mr. Bjelosevic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I can see on the cover is -- I can only read the dates, 12 February 1992 through 27 December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In the course of your visit to Bosanski Samac station and your inspection effectively, did you never ask to see the daily events log-book?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you misunderstood who inspected the organisational units.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ...

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't me. It was the inspectors, according to the lines of work. And when you were talking about the crime investigation department, it was the crime inspector.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I suppose there's not much I can do with this, but do you have any reason to doubt that that is the Samac daily events log-book?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think it calls for speculation. If the witness said he never saw the book --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would you accept - I think that is the most can I take on this document -- would you accept that Samac, the police station, the SJB there, was actually working throughout the period the 12th of -- well, this book is the 12th of February through until the 27th of December?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 12th of February?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know -- well, this initial period, yes, February. But the initial period -- or, rather, the second half of April --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- May, June, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how things functioned there then. But --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I find -- I don't know. I haven't seen this and I really wouldn't want to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you have never ever, ever checked at any stage, through all the fuss and botheration about Todorovic, the daily events log-book. That's effectively what you're saying, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not only that I didn't directly look at the books in Samac. I didn't look at the books directly in any station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'll move on then. That's all I want to ask you about Samac. I want to ask you about the dismissal of Obren Petrovic. Now you said to the Court when you came back that you wanted to deal with that in closed session or in private session, I should say. I want to show you one document. Let's see how we go from there, shall we?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we have up, please, document 65 ter 20128, tab 84A. Now can we go, please, in it to the third page in English and also in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that your signature and stamp?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you have a copy of this document at home?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The documents I had I brought. I cannot recall this coming from me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, we can barely hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. My fault again. Microphone. Your Honours, this document was actually acquired, as I said to the Court, after the Court adjourned on the last occasion when Mr. Bjelosevic finished his evidence in-chief. Can we go back, please, to the front page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is a letter addressed to the minister, is that right, to the Ministry of Interior which, at that stage, had gone to Bijeljina. And it's obviously in 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it lists the complaints. It's the recommendation that Petrovic should be removed. And it lists the matters that are complained about. And I'd like to go, please, to the second page in English --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm really sorry because on the page that we were looking, I note that the parts are missing from the English translation. Namely, the number and the date on the first page are missing from -- if we can have the first page, please, back.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It is back. It's on the screen. Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The English translation doesn't contain the number and the date of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It should be to the left from the official secret, strictly confidential, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's fine. And it's dated the 12th of January, 1993. I'm going to ask for this document to be fully admitted at the end, Your Honours. We'll send it back for a corrected translation. Can we go then, please, to the second page in English again, and I believe that the first -- yes. Stay on the first page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Don't worry about your diary, Mr. Bjelosevic, I'm not interested in the meeting. It's the contents of the document. One of the complaints is at the bottom of the page in B/C/S but at the top of the page in English: "Appointed and placed managers in the police without running the necessary checks or acquiring the approval of the centre chief, some of whom were professional criminals." Now, Mr. Bjelosevic, according to you, for two months you were out of contact with the CSB. It didn't exist. And he and you were off with the military. Wasn't it slightly hypothetical, if I can put it that way, to complain that he had appointed people without consulting you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said he and I. You mean Petrovic, that he was in the military as well? I don't know who you meant when you said that I and he were --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I didn't say that. I'm slightly concerned also about translation.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the interpretation I received, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's in the record, "And he and you ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it's all right. Mr. Zecevic, please. I understand there is a problem with interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I will repeat the question: You complain in this document to the minister and various other people that he appointed people to the police without your approval.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we take a careful look at this document, first, we have to see what its heading says, and we should say, therefore, what the subject is, and then we will see that these are excerpts from a record, from minutes, that were compiled at a meeting that was attended by certain persons. You see that down here, "the meeting was attended by," and then the attendees are listed. So this is a summary of the meeting of all the discussion that took place. So your statement to the effect that on this occasion or by way of this document I am complaining or something is not the case. This is it an excerpt from the minutes and all the discussions are contained there.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said, and what is the way it was, is what is contained here in my notebook.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you wish for us to discuss this in detail, point by point, I stand ready.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I don't, Mr. Bjelosevic. Not for one moment do I wish to do that. I want to ask you about two parts. So are you saying it was not you that made the complaint that he had appointed people to the police without the checks or getting your approval. Somebody else said that. That's -- just requires a yes or no. Doesn't require anything else.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to. As far as the document is concerned, I just wanted to draw your attention to what the subject of the document is. And what the document is entitled. As far as my complaints are concerned with regard to the behaviour of Obren Petrovic at the time, I can deal with that point by point, and I sent this to the minister. What is contained in my notebook, that is mine; whereas this pertains to all the participants in the meeting. That is why I suggest that we make a distinction between the two. My position, my remarks and my proposal, the explanations are all there; whereas this is a discussion, or rather, a record of the discussion that all the participants in the meeting participated in. I had some objections, and I know to this day who could be found in the service, especially in the ranks of the reserve police, to this day, I object to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Now please, Mr. Bjelosevic, answer my question yes or no: Did you make the complaint, as is recorded in these minutes, that he had appointed people to the police without the checks or your approval? That's all I want to know.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. People were received in the reserve police. They were admitted into the reserve police and the station, apart from prescribed procedures, rules and criteria.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I -- I -- I've asked the question three times. You don't want to answer it. We'll move on. The next -- one of the other complaints was, through their inexplicable actions, extracted imprisoned Muslims and Croats, and for money, transfer them to the Federal Republic of Serbia, and then this: "Retained two female workers of Muslim ethnicity which resulted in the justified revolt amongst the fighters." Was it your view that he should not retained in the police station two female workers of Muslim ethnicity or was it somebody else's?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think, Your Honours, I suggest that we should go in private session about this answer. And just one more note.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The witness -- I'm sorry, Ms. Korner. 37/22, the witness said "yes" to the question. The question is: "Did you make the complaint as he recorded in these minutes that he had appointed people to the police without the checks on your approval? That's all I want to know. "A. Yes, people were received ...," and then it goes on. And then the comment by Ms. Korner: "I have the question three times. You don't want to answer it. We'll move on." It is clear that the witness answered and explained. Now I think we should go in a private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't think it's a matter for Mr. Zecevic to decide whether or not we go into private session. It's a matter for this witness with an explanation, Your Honours, why we should be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I was just about to say the same thing, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you want to go into private session, Mr. Bjelosevic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, Your Honours, purely and simply, in order for him to say why he wants to be in private session, I suggest we go into private session. But no other answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we go into private session to get the answer that I would invite Ms. Korner to phrase the question again, once we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, I will repeat the question: Was it you who complained that he had retained Muslim workers which had resulted in a justified revolt?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I wished to explain this, how things went at the meeting, in private session. But it seems to me that that is not being allowed, how this wording came to be --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right, well --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in the first places.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Any further explanation, Mr. Zecevic, who wants to take it from you, can in-chief [sic]. My question is simply that: Are you prepared to say who it was who made that remark in open session?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would leave this for private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Finally, on this document: "Those present unanimously adopted the following conclusions: The CSB chief propose appointments and they be in accordance with the representative of the authorities in politics that an interview be conducted with the SJB chief and that he be confronted with all the failures." Did you conduct an interview with Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is happening? I didn't hear half of the interpretation. Could you please repeat the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. The -- the -- the -- the document goes on that you signed to suggest that an interview be conducted with the SJB chief and that he be confronted with all the failures hampering the further work of the Doboj SJB. Did you conduct an interview with Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Chief Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, with Chief Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke to him after this and before this meeting, too, several times. And after this meeting, I did talk to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you, during the course of this meeting, tell him that he was being removed because it was thought that he was being too friendly with Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, no. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is ... well, let it remain for private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do ask that this document which was referred to by Mr. Petrovic, but it took a long time to get a hold of it, it was only received, as I say, the Monday, I think it is now two weeks ago. So may I ask that that be fully admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, you were about to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, there is a standing objection, Your Honours, and I think we agreed that all the new documents where we object will not be admitted but MFI'd until we make our submissions concerning the fresh evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, so it be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2339, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to turn now to the 11th of July meeting. You, as we have already seen, recorded that on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, just for the -- for the -- for the record, the Registrar 41/1 -- 42/1, Exhibit P2339. It should say "marked for identification." Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 11th of July. We've seen that you had on the 10th of July, a meeting of your SJB chiefs in preparation for the 11th of July meeting. And you've already been taken through, by Mr. Krgovic, your entry for the 11th of July meeting in Belgrade. Is there a reason why you didn't record -- you recorded some of what Zupljanin said. Is there any reason why you didn't record his remarks, even in a sentence, about the prison camps that were being run in Prijedor by the police?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know how things are when you are taking handwritten notes yourself while someone is speaking. Some things you manage to jot down, you miss others, and my priority were the problems that I wished to speak about. In passing, I tried to jot down the problems in the other centres. So there's no problem involved there, in terms of why some things are written down and others are not. Some things I managed to write down; others I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. But you were having the same problem, weren't you, in Doboj, in that, you know, people were being held by police in centres which were not official prisons?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I had to say, I said at the meeting then, and that is contained in the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, according to you, on the 12th of July, you stayed on in Belgrade to have a meeting with Mico Stanisic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the meeting on the 11th of July, we spent the night in Belgrade, and, on the next day, with regard to specific problems, we had the opportunity to meet the representative of the national security, with the head of the sector for national security, and where there was the head of the sector for public security, he spoke to the assistant, at the time the under-secretary in charge of public security, and we had discussions along those lines on the next day. I think that with the minister, I briefly presented the Teslic problems on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the chief of sector of the state security or national security, he stayed considerably longer with the under-secretary for state security. After that was over, we met up and went back to Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When was that meeting? In the morning?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think we met up at that villa around 11.00, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So what time were you back in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when the chief of national security was done, he stayed considerably longer at his meeting. Then we went to lunch, and then we left some time in the afternoon. I don't know what time it could have been.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So were you back in Doboj by 6.30 in the evening?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what time it was. But it was just before sunset, dusk. I really don't know what time it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, that time of year, that would make it later than 6.30, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if we take into account the fact that it is summertime, it was probably later, but I know that we came at dusk. And before Doboj, there was fighting, and there were quite a few wounded and killed. And I know that I went to the hospital to see the wounded up there, and I saw Nenad Kujundzic then who was already in a coma.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was taken to Banja Luka, and he never came to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Don't worry about that. How is it that in this important series of meetings that you had on the 12th of July, there's not a single note in your diary? It is completely blank.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am telling you, if the chief of national security had a meeting with his boss, in terms of his line of work, then he wrote that down. I don't see how this series of meeting crops up all of a sudden. I never mentioned a series. I said that I met up with the minister briefly. And I asked that I be allowed to explain briefly what I know about the Teslic case, since I was the one who presented those problems, I didn't write it down, and I already told you that the head of state security -- no, national security, as it was called at the time, had a longer meeting with his superior. So there was no series of meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You didn't record anywhere, do you, in your diary, that you had a meeting with the minister or with the representatives of the national security sector. It's completely blank that page, isn't it? Don't -- it's as simple as that, isn't it? There is no entry.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if you understood me properly --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes -- no, I understand your explanation.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- or if it was interpreted correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understood your explanation. But you had a meeting with the minister, had you a meeting with national security. You did not record anything in your diary, did you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the under-secretary for national security, it wasn't me who had a meeting with him, but it was the chief of national -- the national security department from Doboj. Could that have been misinterpreted? I think I stated that clearly enough earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You know exactly why this is important, don't you, Mr. Bjelosevic, because on the 12th of July, the Petro Dan [phoen], there occurred in Doboj an attack, didn't there?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've just said as much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Started at about 6.30 in the evening and a number of Muslim prisoners were taken out and used as human shields, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah. You not only heard about it, I suggest, Mr. Bjelosevic, you were involved in it. Because you instructed the police that a human shield should be used but should be -- human shields, I should -- but should be treated humanely?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but what you have just said is simply not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you look for a moment, please, at -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just give me one moment. I've just lost my note.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 20034, please, tab 97.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, what is the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is a newspaper apparently called "Alternativa." And it's an interview with Major Stankovic, and he is being asked about the events of Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you read the article at the time it came out?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember I did. Could it be enlarged?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we -- yeah, somebody has asked for it to be enlarged. Can we try to get into --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I can probably give you a hard copy of it ... [indiscernible] Now I want you --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we go, please, to the second page in B/C/S, and to the third -- sorry. Sixth page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, it's not a great copy, I agree. Is there a bit there headed: "Paying the butcher's bill for Saint Peter's Day"?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was Saint Peter's Day --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're going to ask me about this, let me read it first.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I just want to know -- certainly I will. Was Saint Peter's Day the 12th of July?
