utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'd like you to read, please, then that part --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which part of the text?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Underneath: "Paying the butcher's bill for Saint Peter's Day." I can give you a --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mine's marked, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Ooh, this is very small print.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. It may be easier on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Bjelosevic, all I want to ask you about is one sentence: Is it right, as Mr. Stankovic alleged in this newspaper interview, that on that day, the 12th of July, after arriving in Doboj, in agreement with you, and owing to the critical situation at Vila, he sent Predrag or Predo's Wolves into battle?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Because according to you, you weren't in Doboj on 12th of July; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't until the evening hours and we didn't speak about this. This statement is not true, that we spoke on that day and that he consulted me about Predo's Wolves. That is positively untrue. I don't know where this came from.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But, you see, the evidence that we've had says that it was police officers who used these men as human shields, or took them out and used them as human shields. Are you saying they did this without any order at all from you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most certainly not from me. I heard various versions and accounts of these events, but I don't know what is true. Now I've read this too, but this certainly is not true. I don't know where this story came from.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. We can leave that document. We can leave the topic of the 11th of July and the human shields incident. And can we move, please, generally, to the paramilitary aspect, a little bit more about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, I'm sorry, but the document that you were referring to about the 11th of June, it was, or May, that Mr. Krgovic was leading the witness through, was that tab 5 of Mr. Krgovic's binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: 11th of July, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think so, Your Honours. I'll just check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And if so, it has not been tendered. We do agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, it's not tab 5, it's tab -- oh yes, it is tab 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It has not been tendered, if I'm not wrong.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh. I thought it had been tendered by Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I don't think so. But I can be wrong.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If not, Your Honour, then certainly I'd wish to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... document, Ms. Korner, referred to at page 42/9 -- 10 and 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I can be of assistance, Your Honours. I believe it is Ms. Korner's tab 107D. That's the diary of -- dated the 11 July.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... if it is not tendered by Mr. Krgovic - I assumed it had been - then I will tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... now it does. 107D is not tendered either. So we could give it an exhibit number under this tab number -- under this number, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... I supposed it should have gone in as a Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: As a Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I can't turn it on. Right. Your Honours, if it wasn't tendered by Mr. Krgovic, and despite the fact he gave it a 2D number -- oh, he is saying he did tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Did he?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... all diaries, so that's why I didn't ask them to tender -- that was my point. So I support that it should be tendered, all diary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I'm going to object to the whole diary going in, just the page numbers that are actually referred to, because it becomes impossible, if nobody has ever gone through an entry. So there's a submission Mr. Krgovic can make, if he wants to, but that's objected to. So shall we make the individual, please, an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: As Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It should be 65 ter 20103.04 which is tab 107D, and it should be the P number ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But it's the very same document, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, but did we give it a P number.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All others have been given the P numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And I don't have an objection. I mean ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's just get admitted under whatever number is necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, we are -- there is a slight classification problem that we're trying to resolve. The -- you had indicated that for your purposes, you would have wished to put the whole diary in, and Ms. Korner has recorded her objection. In terms of the particular page that is now before us, the issue is whether it should be identified as a -- as a Defence exhibit or a Prosecution Exhibit. And, Ms. Korner, we're trying to remind ourselves as to what we have done heretofore, in terms of these pages. Can you remind me?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I don't know -- I hadn't appreciated that Mr. Krgovic had not made any of them exhibits on the grounds that he was going to ask for the whole diary to be moved, which did he not ask at the time he finished his cross-examination. So if none of them have gone into evidence, then forgetting about -- well, I mean, are they uploaded into e-court under a Defence number because if they are, then it will have to be the Defence number which becomes a Prosecution Exhibit, or are they uploaded under a Prosecution 65 ter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: No, under --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Under Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]... Defence 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, it better be the Defence number that becomes a P exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I'm hearing Mr. Smith because we have had this slight problem before. It should go under a Defence number, apparently because it is Mr. Krgovic who referred to it first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Are you talking now about an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Defence exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Defence exhibit number, yeah. Otherwise it does lead to horrible confusion. It has a Defence 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I fear that as well. I think it would be simpler to classify it as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D138, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just for the purposes of the clear record, can the Registrar please read the 65 ter number of this document which has been admitted as Exhibit 2D138.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I have it. If I'm not wrong, it is it 2D011169. 2D10 -- sorry, 1169. 2D101169.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, we have just looked at Predrag's Wolves being used. And you identified, which I'm not going to ask you to look at again, a document where you ordered the arrest of the so-called Luis Group, should they materialise in Doboj, which was 1D00466, but I don't want it up. I want you to look, please, at a report done by Colonel-now-General Tolimir, at P591, tab 39B. Have you seen this report by Colonel Tolimir dated the 13th of August before?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say before I look at the document and read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Sorry, it's 28th of July although it's -- all right. Well, just look at the front page, please, and tell us whether you've seen it before.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember having seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I just want to ask you about one part of it. It mentions the Luis Group at page --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm -- I'm terribly sorry to interrupt you, Ms. Korner. It's just not our day. The LiveNote has stopped on my ... on my monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We're three minutes short of the break. We may as well take the break at this point and come back --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've lost all together about half an hour today. We can sit till late and over this business of checking the note. I wonder if I could have an extra half-hour today, if that's possible because I will definitely conclude.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Tacked on to the end of the very-end-of-the-day session?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We'll hear the Defence response of the -- over the break, the usual inquiries could be made.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much. Then I will definitely conclude my examination-in-chief today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: While the witness is on his way in, I believe that counsel and everyone else has been alerted that we will sit straight through until 2.15.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours we have, and I'm very, very grateful to everybody, Your Honours, and counsel, and the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And, of course, the accused.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And them too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Mr. Bjelosevic, I just wanted you to have a look, please, at one part of this document. It talks -- or two parts. Page 3 in English, and page 3 also in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both are in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, you're getting it now. Do you see the paragraph at the bottom in B/C/S, talking about the war staff in Banja Luka, then Nikodin Cavic, finally and then we see war staffs were formed, one for Modrica is headed by Dusan Tosic, aka Luis. Is that the same Luis that you were talking about in that document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably. Having read this, it's becoming clearer to me why Nikodin Cavic and a couple of armed men were chasing me around. Now I am -- it's dawning on me how this was part of the system.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. And can we now look, please, in English at page 5. And in B/C/S, at page 5 as well. The paragraph in English is the third one; and in B/C/S, it is the fourth, or fifth, which begins: "A special police unit under the command of a certain Kujundzic has been established in the village of Stanari in the municipality of Doboj ... consists of about 80 men who are mainly involved in setting up check-points which they use for their criminal activities." Is that Predrag's Wolves?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If Predo's Wolves are meant, then two things are wrong here. Namely, the village of Stanari, because that's not where they are from; and I don't think they had as many men. They must have had fewer than this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. And it says it's a special police unit. And it was a special police unit, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, well, I don't know what kind of idea individual people have about the special police. It's a fact that if we're talking about Predo's Wolves, for a while, they were members of the reserve police of the Doboj SJB. That's -- that much is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. So what is described by everybody as a paramilitary organisation was actually part and parcel of the MUP, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only for a certain time-period. If it is important, let me say they were established, or mobilised, as a military unit. And they were members of the military for a part of May, as far as I remember, early May. Then they became renegades and acted autonomously on their own. Later, they joined the reserve police for a time-period.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, you see, what I want to know, Mr. Bjelosevic, is why? You issued this order to arrest Luis's group. Why aren't you issuing orders to rest this man's group?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that question should be put to Chief Petrovic to answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But you're back in Doboj by July when they're still operating, because we've just seen that. Why didn't you issue the order as the chief of the CSB?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a later period, the station chief decided about reserve police stations, one of which was at Suho Polje. That's the area of Ozren where they were located and they were the staff of the reserve police station at Suho Polje. And if I understood correctly, that's one of the reasons why I wanted to remove Chief Petrovic to have him replaced.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So the fact that nothing was done about removing these criminals from the Doboj police ranks is, again, due to Petrovic and not you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if you understood what I was saying correctly. I was warning Petrovic about that, and more than once, he expressed fear. He said he was afraid of them. And, finally, he adopted such a decision that he transferred them to the reserve police at Suho Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you look, please, at document which is part of the Defence documents, which is Defence 00212 -- 00212D1, I think. And it's Defence tab 100. I can't remember whether it was made an exhibit or not, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could the usher please give the binder to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Not an exhibit. All right. Your Honours, the English translation is not going to help much, but -- because they don't list all the names.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But does this say this is a submission of individual lists of wounded and killed persons. And if we look at the last page in English and the last page in B/C/S, is that signed by you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if we then, please, go back in B/C/S - and it won't help anywhere else, I am afraid, in English, to page 1, 2, 3, 4 -- 3. And if we highlight number 30, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's page 2 then.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, page 2 in -- on the top. We've got it on the screen. Is that Predrag Kujundzic, who we've just been talking about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a Defence document, so I take it there's no objection to this being admitted an exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: This is a list of killed and wounded members of CSB Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2340, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, can I just check one thing in my notes. Yes. Same topic. Could we have tab 60 -- sorry. Tab 68 in our bundle, not in the Defence bundle. And it's document 20020.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Clearly, this man is still alive in August. And on the 28th of September, apparently information is being sent to inform the CSB Doboj that Mr. Kujundzic, a worker of CSB Doboj, acquired for himself and his group, 70 kilos of jewellery, foreign money and in the course of cleansing of the village of Civcije, the municipality -- his group handed 350.000 German marks to him. And it's all about looting. Did you get this report, Mr. Bjelosevic, in September?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive this. At least I do not remember having received it. But I did receive certain notes that indicate their criminal activity, and this came from several sources, the security organs of the military, and some inspectors. But this, I do not recall having received. I received information also through observations. There's a lot to be said. I don't know how interesting it is. Precisely because they knew that I was making efforts to have them eliminated from the reserve milicija. There were threats. There were -- they were trying to agree on having me assassinated. I did not bring any of these notes here, but there was knowledge to that effect, and I had been warned directly, as well. For a while, I did not even sleep at my own apartment --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a dangerous group.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So you -- were you aware even if you say you didn't get this document, were you aware of the information contained therein?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, never, until now. I think I did not hear of these quantities of gold and jewellery. But they had vehicles where their reserve police station was. There was knowledge to that effect. It was documented, too. On one occasion, I asked the chief of the station to establish that directly and to see what was there and what was not there, but I never received that. He always said that he was afraid of them and that it is best for them to be there, that they are the least dangerous over there, and that is where they are the most peaceful.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But we saw in connection with the Luis Group that the military had been involved in trying to arrest them as well, which is why you were sending out that notice. Why, if this was such a dangerous group and you needed to great rid of them, arrest them, didn't you ask for assistance from the military?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I tell you that Predrag Kujundzic put a pistol against Major Stankovic's head, perhaps the answer will come to you straightaway. Numerically, they were far stronger than Luis's Group. And Luis's Group was more brutal, yes, but there were fewer of them there, and it was easier to overcome them in that location where they were. So both reasons worked in favour of that being done. Don't think that assessments were not being made. They were. However, it would have been very bloody if someone wanted to have a showdown with them, arrest them or do anything of the kind. Attempts were made to put parts of them in the military --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- when they were located in Suho Polje, part of them went to the army. The entire teem team was not together, the entire unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, do I understand this correctly, and again this can be answered very simply yes or no, the combined police force in Doboj and the combined military together, were not able to arrest this man and his group; is that right? They were frightened.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could have been done probably, but the question is: What the price would be and how many casualties would be involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can I ask then you finally, two further documents on this topic of personnel in the police. Could you have a look please at 2D89 MFI'd, which is at tab 14E. It's not in your bundles, Mr. Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this the one, the document we keep having an argument with Mr. Krgovic. So the new translation is not in e-court, but we'll put it in Sanction, because, at the moment, as you remember, Mr. Krgovic wants CLSS to have another go at translating it. So it's in Sanction, please, this translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, this is, Mr. Bjelosevic, again, a payroll for the CSB Doboj, 5th Company -- no, sorry, I'm looking at the wrong one. It's not. It's a payroll ... for the 9th Company for special assignments. But it's headed: "Doboj." And can you identify the signature at the bottom? I think it's a familiar one.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the beginning of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I recognise the signature in the middle. It is mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's yours; right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, and, indeed, we can see --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I don't know whose signature the one on the right side is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. And we can see that the -- the first.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Ms. Korner. This is the third time that the interpreters didn't hear part of the answers. I didn't intervene before. I didn't want to ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What answer? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It says: "The interpreter did not hear the beginning of the sentence."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I asked you can you identify the signature at the bottom. I think it was a familiar one. And then you started to give an answer, and the interpreter didn't hear the beginning of the sentence. Does it matter? He has given the answer.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the bottom, in the middle down there, that is my signature, where the stamp is. I cannot recognise the one on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, one of the people listed there at number 14, I think, is -- is that Nikola Grgic. No, further down. It's the one -- yes, the one before the bottom. Sorry. It's that one, yep.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 14 is some Ranko.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. It's number 18. Is that Grgic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nikola is the father's name; Aleksander is his name. But I cannot see the last name very well, the one on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us why it was that you were sending to Banja Luka -- or why the 9th Company for special assignments Banja Luka had something to do with Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I answered this question, if I remember correctly, earlier on. It has to do with members of this unit who were with the inspectors, who were operatives from state security -- or, rather, national security, who came from Banja Luka and provided assistance to the national security in Doboj. I think that we've already discussed this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, can we have look, please, at the next page in B/C/S. Not in English. Is that Slobodan Karagic again at the top?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's quite illegible. Really is illegible.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So going back to the front page --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is this right: That you are paying for the services of people who came from Banja Luka, and this is being sent back apparently to Banja Luka? Or is it the other way around? Are you asking them to pay?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is most illegible. But I think you said page 1 and 2. I think that the document that you displayed previously does not comprise a whole together with this one, if I noted its content correctly as well as the signatures, et cetera. However, the question was whether that was the case -- well, I think that they, I mean, these on this list, had been paid a compensation for May for their stay in Doboj. That this payment was made by -- I don't know whose signature this is on the right-hand side. Now is it Dervenic, I'm not sure. I think that's what happened. I think, I assume, I cannot say with 100 per cent certainty.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I don't want to ask you anything more about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness identified his signature. I don't know how long we are going to go on MFI'ing this, but at some stage it's got to be made an exhibit, a proper one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problem is that the translation is not complete. And that is why there was this objection by the Prosecutor because we still haven't got a full translation of this document. Once again, we have a problem, Your Honours. This document that I'm interested in is only the first page. The rest are parts of another document. They are not one and the same document. So this first page that was displayed is a document that we were interested in and that we wanted to have translated. The remaining pages are not part of this document. They are different documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours it's no good Mr. Krgovic asserting this. If he wants to call evidence about that, that's one thing, but at the moment these are all part and parcel of the same document. Anyhow, let's not waste time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to because the witness just said that, that this first document is not one and the same document with the rest, that these are different documents ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's move on, please. Can we look finally, please, on this issue, very quickly, at document 24 bis, which is -- tab 24 bis, which is P1300. Thank you. E-court has collapsed again, has it? Oh, I see. We have to go back -- sorry. Can we go back to e-court? We're in Sanction at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. This is a May document from Doboj. And if we look, please - it's a long list - in -- I don't think the English will help much, but it's the fourth page in B/C/S, under the heading of -- I think it's -- is it special platoon? Is that special platoon?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Above number 83, it says "special platoon within the company."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And is number 83, Nikola Jorgic? And number --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And 97 and 98, Slavko Spasojevic and Slobodan Tekic, are they two of the people who went into Teslic as part of the Mice group?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I think that it's those people, but I would like to ask, if it's not a problem, to call up the previous page again. There is something important for me. Could I please have a look again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Do you mean the first -- the very first page?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that one. The one that we saw as the first page. Before this last one? Well, all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see it here as well. It's the heading up here or the letterhead that confuses me a bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. It says CSB Doboj, 5th Company --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 5th Company of the milicija.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't you see that something else was here? Before Doboj? And that that was crossed out and then CSB is on the left? If I see this right ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I do. And is there a point you want to make on that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, yes, of course I do. Because the centre did not have a single company of its own, let alone five of them. I think this has to do with the station and that it's been changed or doctored. Take a look.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes because it doesn't --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to see who signed this. There you go. If that's not a problem. If we could go to the end of the document to see whose signature is there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There is no signature. Somebody has put chief --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ah, then I --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there's no signature on the side to the effect that the money had been collected. I don't see what kind of probative value this can have, but these are my observations.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It doesn't exactly, Mr. Bjelosevic, does it, agree with your theory or your -- I'm sorry, not theory, I apologise, assertion that the CSB Doboj was not operating for three months.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say three. It is well known which period this is, but I think --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the end of the sentence. I'm afraid it's my fault. I had the microphone on. What were you saying?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this document confirms what I've been saying. That these are not the forces of the centre but of the station, rather.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to move, please, briefly from this topic to the question of legal measures. Your Honours, Mr. Zecevic had, as part of the documents he showed this witness, which was a copy of which was provided to the witness, document at tab 215. He asked for it to be admitted, and we objected. We -- we withdraw the objection. To save me having to asking the witness about it, could I simply ask that it be admitted. The document number --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I can help with you that Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 389D1. And it was our tab number 215.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it deals with part of the matters that I wanted to ask him about, but he has already dealt with that, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I offered this document. Ms. Korner objected. It wasn't admitted. Now we should -- it is my understanding that now Ms. Korner wants to have this document admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So I pray that this document be given 1D number.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's a list of unidentified perpetrator cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D542, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, the -- Mico Stanisic issued an order on the 23rd of July, which I am not going to ask you to look at because I know you're familiar with it, saying that --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we lost the LiveNote again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We're advised that's a problem that is going to continue in and out for the rest of the day. When it goes out, it would come back in within ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it's on the main screen, Your Honours. I see it's just on our computer screens that it has gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, it effectively creates a big problem for me for the re-direct. But I will, I guess -- I will need to lead with this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's come back. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That police officers who were alleged to have committed criminal offences should be suspended and put at the disposal of the military. I'm sure you recall that order.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall that. There were several orders from the minister to that effect to cleanse the ranks of the active force and the reserve force. Cleanse the ranks of all of those who committed criminal offences and violations, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You never, in fact, launched criminal proceedings against any police officer in Doboj for crimes committed against non-Serbs, did you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. But there were such instances, yes. I don't know in which year, but there were some.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm talking -- I'm talking about -- for offences committed in 1992.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the time when the -- when the criminal reports were filed, not about the time when the offences were committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Criminal reports filed in 1992 against police officer -- people who were listed on the police payrolls for crimes committed against non-Serbs. Now, if you can't remember, say so.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember when the criminal reports were filed, but there obviously were some criminal reports and proceedings were instituted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting there weren't any against police officers altogether, simply for committing crimes, such as looting, killing, beating of non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how I understood you. Yes, there were some for such offences, too. There were some criminal reports and proceedings for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us when and where?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I might make a mistake when I specify the year. But I remember well that there was a police officer who was member of the special detachment. He was deprived of liberty after his offence because he had killed some Muslims. But that can be found. It may have been in 1994 or -- but proceedings were instituted. There's no doubt about that. And the relevant document can be found in the archives.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Sorry, that's 1994 for a killing committed in 1992; or 1994 for a killing committed in 1994?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, well, I don't know for sure. But as you were able to see from the documents displayed here, these are criminal reports, that an on-site investigation was carried out on the occasion of each killing. There were statements taken from witnesses, but when any individual case was subsequently dealt with, I cannot say. We would need additional documentation to be precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I want you to look, please, at one entry in the Doboj criminal report, the KU, for the SJB Doboj, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that is 65 ter 10353, I hope. And it's at tab 104. Sorry, it's 39A quater. Sorry, wrong tab.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, are you referring to the KU register?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think it is 1D358, and it's -- the tab is 245 in the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: SJB Doboj, KU.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it was recorded as 58. I said 1D358.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's not a D, as far as I know. It's never been ... Sorry, it's -- that's what I thought. It's tab 104, 65 ter what? 20100. Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just before we look at that, can you tell us the name, please, of the police officer who was charged with killing Muslims? I forgot to ask you that.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I mean, this was an unusual -- sorry, you wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was the name again? Well, all we need to do is make a phone call and then we'll get the name and the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you recognise this book?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recognise it, but I can see what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. And do you accept that this is the crime report book for the SJB Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "OSUP Doboj" in the upper left-hand corner, although the label is torn.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, if you just go to the next page, I think can you see clearly that it's the SJB Doboj. Can we try and ... [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, last week sometime, I was asking you questions about voting in the plebescite and the referendum. And you said that was everyone's right to vote in the plebescite for the Serbs, or the referendum for the -- that was held by the BiH government. Do you remember talking about that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you see -- I'm just going to have to find the pages. There should be a list of charges against some people called Begovic and a whole load of others. Can you -- unfortunately, I now can't find the reference to them. July of 1992, so let me just ... ah, found it. Can we go, please, to the page at the top. I have no idea what the page number is, but it should say 0665-1438.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is still page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, can we go, please. You have to go -- so that's 16. So it's about another 22 pages on.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. No, it's coming, I hope. Yes, can we -- can we go to the right-hand side so that we can see if it's -- can we go to the -- no. Reduce it, thank you. Is that 1438? You're right. Now, can you now enlarge it, please, so that the first ... Is that a series of people listed, starting with Nedzad Begovic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can this be enlarged some more? I cannot read it. Could you please zoom in. The numbers are in column 1 and it begins with number 21.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's number -- it should be number 26, it is, actually, I think.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, all right, who's --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ahmic. I think the first name is Mehmed Alija, if I can see it well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Anyhow, I agree, it's not a very good copy, and regrettably we haven't got -- Do you see there's a whole list of people on that page. And if we see the offence, which is -- well, we can see it there. Begovic. In English, anyhow. This is taking too long. Do you see an entry for Avdic, Avdic, Ahmic, Kadric, Prijanic, Tokmanovic, Dudic, Kopljar, et cetera, et cetera, and then Begovic is number 13.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This ends with number 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, okay. I think this may be the wrong page, regrettably. It's page 26 in B/C/S. No, no, no --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the top there is Vahid Begovic. Under number 13. Is this it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's not. I'm not going to trouble with this anymore because this is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we remove that, please, from the screen and could we put up, please, the document which is at 39A quater, which is 1 -- which should be, I hope, 65 ter 10353.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is a criminal report dated -- in fact, it should be the 27th of July, I think we can all see in the B/C/S, and it's obviously in the book at 13292, but never mind, against Mr. Begovic and a number of others, huge number of others, including Mr. Krnic. If we go, please, in English, page 14 in English. And it's page 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. Seven in B/C/S. No, it's not. In B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see that name here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no, no. You're quite right, because it's not the right page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we go -- it should say page 10 in B/C/S at the top, page 10 in type. It should be one -- after the page you've got up, three pages further on in B/C/S. Three pages further on. Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, can you see the second name down there?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Krnic born in 1912.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mijat Krnjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now can we look, please, at what all these men were actually charged with. If we go to the next page in English. And it's the same page -- sorry. It's the same page in English, I think, as well. Sorry, it's the same page in English: "There are reasonable grounds to suspect that the subjects committed the crime of threatening territorial integrity under Article 116 in wanting to use unconstitutional means to break off parts of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and annex them to another state. "Namely, on 29 February and 1 March 1992, according to their statements ... the aforementioned subjects took part in a referendum and voted for a sovereign unitary and independent Bosnia and Herzegovina." I'm not going to take you through the whole report, but many inspectors were committed to -- and interviewing all of these. Was that a proper criminal report, in your view, Mr. Bjelosevic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would now have to see what exactly this article of the penal code of SFRY stipulates. But I don't want to offend anybody. However, let me say that no serious person would ever -- or at least suffice it to say, that I, personally, would have never done anything like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, so marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2341, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. I want to deal very briefly with the Mice incident, Mr. Bjelosevic. You would accept, would you not, that the group known as the Mice committed a number of serious crimes in Teslic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Ranging from unlawful arrest?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, and according to the information I have received, there were various offences. But according to that same information, they committed a lot of offences. I don't know the details or which individual did what. I do know that proceedings were instituted. How they ended, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to go into that because the Court has heard evidence about this, Mr. Bjelosevic. But you wrote a number of documents, didn't you, which you have been taken through, haven't you, disassociating yourself completely from these events and blaming Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're putting -- well, let's not go into that. I wrote a number of documents about -- or in accordance with the information I received. I believe that the first document was an Official Note after the event, and after that, there was one more reporter, too, when I received subsequent information about what happened, who went there and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I can give you the dates of your reports, and if you need to see them, you can. 1st of July, 17th of August, and then October 1992. Does that sound right to you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that fits. There were three documents, and that's about the time-frame. The first was an Official Note. The second was a report based on what I learned when Inspector Solaja interviewed them. And the third one followed later.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm going to come in a moment to Inspector Solaja. I just want to ask you about one matter. Is there -- you know that statements were taken in July from all the people who had been involved in the actual Mice incident, don't you, for the purposes of a criminal file.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, as far as I know, an investigation was carried out then. The police was involved there and the public prosecutor and the investigative magistrate, and so on. As far as I know, that's how things went, and I think the result was a criminal report, and I believe that proceedings were initiated.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And presumably you found out that the two -- the SJB chief and the SJB commander, Mr. Kuzmanovic, and Mr. Markocevic, both made statements in early July?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I suppose so. It would only be logical.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would you agree that during the period of the Mice's reign in Teslic, Mr. Markocevic tried to get in touch with you, and, indeed went to see you one day in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, Mr. Perisic and somebody else came to see me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And we met on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm suggesting -- I'm asking you, rather, whether Mr. Markocevic came to see you in Doboj during the course of June, explained the problems in Teslic, and you said that you would talk to Milan Savic. Did anything like that happen?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that anything like that happened. That -- that we discussed this topic? No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Milan Savic was never charged, was he?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. But it seems to me that he -- his name was not included in this criminal report about Teslic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But no. You know -- I mean, that's the whole point, isn't it, Mr. Bjelosevic. You were being blamed. It was said by people that you had sent them, Savic and the rest of them, there, wasn't it? And that's why you spent so long investigating yourself.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. That's not the way it was. I would like to remind you that the investigation was led by the Banja Luka centre and the Teslic station, along with the basic court and prosecutor's office in Teslic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. But you weren't satisfied of all that because you, yourself, wrote a number of reports, Mr. Bjelosevic, as we've just been through. And the reason for you doing all this is because people were saying you were responsible. Wasn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could not have been in charge of the investigation in any way, but I did inquire as to what was going on there. Because if someone wanted to kill me, then I wanted to know why and why I was met that way in Teslic. And it's well known who was carrying out the investigation and who was in charge of the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But it was clear, wasn't it, from everything that you found out and it's in your reports that Mr. Savic was responsible for the police element of this group, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to the statement of those who went up there with Savic, and you could have seen that from the statements, well, yes, he took them there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's look at your own report of the 17th of August, very quickly, please. Which is at tab 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's P1 -- oh, no, let's not. It's been exhibited. It is P1343.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you take any steps, Mr. Bjelosevic, to remove or have removed Mr. Savic from the police in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When assessing that, I was primarily guided by what the investigating team did. Since a criminal report had been not been filed against him, I've already told you that, later -- I told you how actually I gradually came to know different things in this regard. I noticed that there were elements involving his responsibility, and when I was slowly preparing that, in order to be able to carry out disciplinary proceedings, Milan Savic first, I don't know how, left. He was at the public security station for a while, and then he left the service.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Markocevic, however, and Mr. Kuzmanovic were removed as chief and commander of the SJB Teslic, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think they were suspended by Radulovic or whoever was in charge of the proceedings. But they were removed from the duties that they had until then.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Because they had done absolutely nothing to try and stop these men, had they?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what the decision exactly stated, but you know because of local jurisdiction and for -- because of the decision of the municipality. I really do not -- or could not have had any more detailed information in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let's have a look at what you actually did in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we have a look at 65 ter 20014 document, tab number 57. Stamped the 8th of September, 1992. If we go, please, to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that your signature at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we go to the bottom, please. Second page, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Go back on the first page, first page in B/C/S, please. Sorry, second. Sorry. My fault.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that you proposing that Mr. Kuzmanovic and Mr. Markocevic are reinstated after all this as chief and commander of Teslic SJB?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And Marinko Djukic as the third one, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours may that be admitted and marked -- MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P2342, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. You mentioned Inspector Solaja who was doing the inspection of the Mice for you. And you talked about how he had been removed. I'd like you to have a look, please -- sorry, he been disciplined, and I'd like you to have a look, please, at 65 ter 20123, please, tab 78B.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The taking of statements doesn't have anything to do with measures against him, if that's --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, you're quite right. But you did deal with that last time, and you suggested that he had been disciplined for committing offences against non-Serbs. And I just want you to have a look at the actual facts, as they were revealed by the judgement. All right. This is the -- your decision; is that right -- we better look at the -- can we see your signature at the bottom. Yes, we can. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The facts of this are his employment was terminated because, on 8th of November, 1992, he tried to take to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the Mandic family and Mr. Petar Maric, all are Croats; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He tried to take these persons in a vehicle. The documents were forged, and it was all done for money, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But it wasn't committing offences against non-Serbs, was it, which is what you suggested? He was actually helping them, if anything.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, was he helping them? If, in that situation, he took money away from them, I would not agree that that is help. I think it's averous. At that time the International Red Cross had a strong presence there and people could go to the places they wanted to go to through their mediation, so I would not agree that there weren't elements of avers here and that this was assistance. Also documents were forged, too, as far as I can remember the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. No, no, if you look at it --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm sorry. Page 80, line 21, it was recorded as: "A. Well, was he helping them?" I think it was your question, Ms. Korner. Yes, so after that, "if" should be recorded as answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, may this be admitted and marked, please -- MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, at what line is it that part of the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... it's page 80, line 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It was recorded: "A. Well, was he helping them?" And I think that's a question. And then comes the answer: "If, in that situation ..." and so on, "he took the money from them," that's the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... as I understood it, this was said by Mr. Bjelosevic. His answer was: "Well, is that helping." Don't you agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps that's the situation. I'm not sure anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Bjelosevic was questioning the fact that helping -- that assisting persons for money, was that helping them. And he said, no, that was --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. The gist is recorded properly. I was just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I don't know whether -- has it been given a number? MFI?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2343, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to turn briefly to the question of the relationship between you, the police, and the army, and specifically between you and -- and, as he then was, Colonel Lisica, later General Lisica. Do you agree that the principle of the police being resubordinated to the army was actually governed by the Law on National Defence?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I just want to put some propositions to you, please, Mr. Bjelosevic. Firstly, you mentioned Colonel Lisica. You came back to him, in fact, at one stage in the course of your evidence where you said you didn't want to make it sound as though you and Colonel Lisica disagreed. Do you remember saying something like that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is what I said roughly: That I'm not complaining about what he did, because, he, as commander, had the right to order what he ordered, the engagement of forces in areas within his area of responsibility. I think that that is what I said roughly, and that is what I believe to this day.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I think it is slightly more than that, isn't it? The fact is that the police and the military in the Doboj area in particularly [sic] had the same goal in mind. Namely, to get rid of what you described as enemy forces; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what more appropriate word would be if we were at war with each other and if we were firing at each other. It's different now after all these years. At the time, these were warring parties, and if somebody thinks that it was supposed to be called something different, well, I don't because you saw how many casualties there were among the police, not to mention the army, and then in Doboj, say, 90 civilians, yes, they were enemy forces. And it's only natural if we were fighting and we -- we then wanted to defeat them, yes. It's not that they were throwing ice-cream at us and that we were firing bullets at them. No. We fired at them and they fired at us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. See if you agree with this proposition: When a people, when a territory is in danger, practically in danger, that means you have only one task. And that one single task is the defence of the territory and the defence of the people, and there are no conflicting aims, that the police should have one role, and that the military should have another. Do you agree with that proposition?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I referred to that earlier on as well. Defence is the number one priority. Everything else comes after that. That's the way it was according to our laws and the constitution, because the constitution stated that that was the highest duty and responsibility of military-age able-bodied citizens defence. And then also, that was part of the awareness of the people themselves, that that was the topmost task, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Did you have a conversation at any stage with Colonel Lisica where he explained to you and others who were there that it was all very well to say that the police were not a combat force, but that if the enemy took over this territory, then there would be no territory to control? Do you remember having a conversation along those lines with him?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked to him many times and that was at his command post and during briefs, and so on, at the barracks in Derventa, and not to mention all these places in Doboj as well. In Doboj, when he was commander of the operations group, we did talk, but he wrote that to me once in his answer when, because of the deterioration of the security situation, I asked that we get the milicija out of the Brod front line and I explained why. His answer to me was, Yes, I understand your problems, but I do not agree with having the milicija withdrawn because if you remain without a territory, or whatever his words were, if they capture your town, or something like that, you will have no place where you would ensure law and order.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Do you agree with this proposition: There were no clashes between the military and police because the goal was the same. Perhaps we had -- perhaps there were some disputes, but disputes did not transfer into open conflict. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, at least in that area of his responsibility, there was no open conflict between the army and the police. There was one incident between the military police of the 327th Brigade and the milicija from Prnjavor that had been brought to Derventa to do that work --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, that was the only case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... I really don't need this detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, can we -- I didn't want to interrupt either the question or the answer. Can we get the reference from where Ms. Korner is reading these propositions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I am putting propositions to him, but I'm perfectly prepared to say where I'm taking them from, if you want me to [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]... if it is a statement of some kind, then you're obviously trying to get around the Rule 92 [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I'm not. I'm putting --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... that's why I'm asking -- that's why I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I'm putting propositions to him. I would tell you where I get the propositions from, if you really want to know, but I am simply asking him whether he agrees. I am not, in any way, attempting to introduce any statement into evidence. Now, do you want me to tell you from what I am reading in front of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's definitely what I ask you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. This is the interview with General Lisica, which was conducted sometime ago during the break where we had a request from the Defence, having been told by somebody that we had interviewed him that we provide a copy of the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But that is precisely what I suspected you were doing, Ms. Korner. And it was the Office of the Prosecutor's position until very recently that this is a way behind the Rule 92.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, please. It was -- I will find the reference in the transcript. When I wanted to introduce with the previous witness the statement or the court transcript from the Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina, about a previous minister Alija Delimustafic, and it was said that in that case, I would need to bring Alija Delimustafic here to confirm these words. And the same thing you are doing right now. You're trying to introduce the statement of Lisica in this -- in this way, I think. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It is either a deliberate or totally ignorant statement that Mr. Zecevic has just made. I'm not trying to introduce anything. I deliberately did not mention it. I am putting propositions to this witness to see whether he agrees with them. If he doesn't agree with them, then I have a different course to take. It is why exactly I did not point out what it was that I was -- where I was reading it. I am not, in any way -- it is not like Mr. Zecevic attempting to get in a transcript of a witness who -- as part of the evidence. I am simply putting factual matters. And if Mr. Zecevic can't see that, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Please continue, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: While we are on that topic, did you have a conversation with General Lisica before you came to give evidence or during the break?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this break? No, not with anyone. I didn't talk to anyone from that circle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I was going to say, Ms. Korner, perhaps it would be helpful for you to identify to the witness what you mean by "the break."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, yes, you're quite right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: First of all, before you came to give evidence, after February -- between February and when you first came here in April, did you have a conversation with General Lisica?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have General Lisica's number, and he's a man I have a high regard for, and I call him every now and then when I come to Banja Luka. We have a cup of coffee. When I last talked to him, I cannot remember exactly. I would not make a mistake in terms of the date or time. But, yes, I do see the man, yes, from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you see him after he had been interviewed by us in February?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when he was interviewed by you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I'm trying to remember now when it was that I last saw him ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was it you who provided the information to the Defence counsel that we had conducted an interview with him, to either Mr. Zecevic or Mr. Cvijetic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know whether I said something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Do you agree -- let me return to the propositions that I'm putting to you. Do you agree that if there was no agreement between you and the colonel about the use of your men in fighting, you could apply through your chain of command and he through his, to get your superiors to decide the issue?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that happened several times. Already the first meeting, on the 11th of July, we complained to the minister about that situation. So, not about what the commanders did but we were complaining about the situation, that it was hard to endure all of that. It was only natural that I, as someone who was in charge in the internal affairs service that I tried to have as many members of the milicija as possible to be involved in such matters; whereas, the commander wanted to carry out his own task as best he could. So that was an approach that was a bit different. Everybody tried to do whatever they had to do in the best possible way. But, after all, it was well-known who had the say, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But the simple point is that it wasn't a question, however Colonel Lisica phrased himself, of the military simply ordering the police to be doing things, which they didn't want to. It was mutual agreement, wasn't it, between the two of you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree. You cannot reach agreements on something that is written in the law. We can either act in accordance with the law, or not observe the law. An agreement would mean something different.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the law said there had to be formal resubordination, didn't there?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "formal resubordination." But the law prescribes that the commander, the military commander, at brigade level and higher than that, has the right to engage all defence structures within the area of his responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: To make the request; isn't that right, Mr. Bjelosevic? However it was phrased, it was actually a request.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Order.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if, as I -- as I'm putting to you, you refuse, as we know that you did on some occasions, then the -- the question of whether this resubordination was to take place had to go up the chain of command to General Talic or Mico Stanisic, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously you are looking at this in a scholarly way, as it were. This is far removed from the real situation on the ground. There was no time in war to apply all proper procedures. We established a special detachment that was part of the special police brigade of the MUP. It had its headquarters in Doboj. And in case of urgent need, I was able to order the use of this detachment and only subsequently apply for the minister's approval. Or, if there was time, I could ask for his approval in a timely fashion.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. In fact, Mr. Bjelosevic, this was, was it not, a mutually supportive relationship which included you making requests of him and him making requests of you?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, it is quite clear I simply cannot finish today. One last document, please, which is -- it's 20018, tab 65.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, is -- was this a question? Page 90/10 to 12. And does witness need to answer or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask him -- that's why I'm asking him to look at this document. This is a question. Thank you. Can we go to the second page in each, please. Third page in -- in B/C/S, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Document signed by you, Mr. Bjelosevic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Back to the first page --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you show the first page so that I can see the date? Or, actually, it's on this page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... I'm going to send you -- I'm going to show you the first page again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Second page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move on to the text.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Dated 21st September 1992, to the command of the operations group of the Serbian army Doboj. In fact, not to TG3, but the principle is the same. You are asking the army to release these persons to become police officers, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a request for their relief so that they can attend a training course. If I remember correctly --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- these candidates did not leave during the planned period. They were only relieved later and sent to the training course subsequently, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But it matters not, does it? It is an illustration of the principle, I say, where this was a mutually supportive military/police co-operation with the same goal in mind; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if you read this carefully, but I'll get there. These are military conscripts, and the request is made for them to be relieved from their military units so that they could attend a training course. And after that training course, they could become employees of the ministry. If so, if you read carefully, then you were able to see that. And as for your remark -- or, rather, what you are putting to me, of course, we were not supposed to be on confrontation course, the army and the MUP. That's the last thing we needed. Of course, we had good relations and co-operated. What else? We weren't supposed to fight the army, were we? I don't really get the point.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, the point is you were trying to suggest, Mr. Bjelosevic, that you could do nothing because the army moved in, removed all your police, and that was it. And that's just not the way it happened, is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, we have reached the point where we must take the adjournment for the day.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... yes, we have -- I -- yes. Your Honour, I'm so sorry, and I'm sorry to have made you sit longer. I still have a little bit left to deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we would resume at 9.00 tomorrow in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
